messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: propto density summands & unit testing
parts:
I'm in the middle of fixing multi normal and
noticed that there are not enough tests for propto.

You can drop a summand in a log probability if and
only if both

1) propto == true, and
2) there are no stan::agrad::var variables in the
summand

Here's the first summand in the definition of multi_normal:

if (!propto)
lp += NEG_LOG_SQRT_TWO_PI * y.rows()
- 0.5 * log(Sigma.determinant());

This needs to be broken out into:

if (!propto)
lp += NEG_LOG_SQRT_TWO_PI * y.rows();

if (!propto || !is_constant<T_covar>::value)
lp -= 0.5 * log(Sigma.determinant());

I'll add the is_constant<> metaprogramming for
vectors and matrices to support the static tests.

The other conditions need to be refined in the
same way. If we include all the summands, we'll
get the right answer -- it'll only cost us some speed
and memory. So feel free to leave things without
the propto calc -- we can optimize later in a way
that'll be backward compatible.

We will need tests for propto. I think these should
be in the form of log difference tests, exploiting
the fact that we've tested foo<false> (full calc),
and that:

foo<true>(theta1) - foo<true>(theta2)

== foo<false>(theta1) - foo<false>(theta1)

So we can choose some pairs of theta1 and theta2,
then work through all the permutations of var
and constant testing the above.

This'll avoid the need to test exact values of
foo<true> (proportional calc), which may change over
time as we optimize. (It won't if we minimize
the calcs the first time through.)

And the whole reason I dove into the class in the
first place is that we need to replace the direct calls
to Eigen's matrix ops with our own wrappers to take
care of promotion to auto-dif variables (alternatively,
we could promote within the probability calcs, but that
seems less modular).

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] propto density summands & unit testing
parts:
I think it's OK to have unit tests depend on lower-level
functions that are themselves tested. We don't need to
test compound functionality the pieces of which are unit
tested. So just testing that we've defined the probability
densities so they can be auto-diffed is enough -- we don't
need to check the results (of course, it couldn't hurt and
redundant testing with different approaches is in general
a good thing).

There's nothing special about the y in y ~ Foo(theta),
You'll have to include it when it touches the params.
So it's usually still there following the same reules.

For instance, for log Beta(y|alpha,beta):

summand include if variable
1) - log B(alpha,beta) alpha | beta
2) + (alpha - 1) log(y) alpha | y
3) + (beta - 1) log(1 - y) beta | y

Here (1) is a pure normalizing term only involving the
distribution arguments, but y touches the parameters
in terms (2) and (3). The big savings is if alpha and
beta are constant, because (1) involves log gamma functions
and derivatives digamma functions as well.

- Bob

PS: I'm on my way into the office.
